questions.question: What was the main form of property in the Rig Veda?
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is Cow . Key Points The Cow was the main form of property of the Rig Vedic people . Most of the wars in the Rig Vedic period were fought for the sake of Cows . War is referred to as ' gavishthi ' in the Rig Veda. "Gavishthi" means to search for Cow. Cows were also given as gifts to priests. Rig Vedic: Rig Vedic Aryans used the cost of mail and helmet in warfare whereas the people of Indus Valley Civilization did not leave any evidence of using them.

questions.question: How many Mahajanpadas were there in ancient India?
questions.solution: Solution: The Correct Answer is  16 . During the lifetime of Lord Gautam Buddha, sixteen Mahajanpadas existed in the 7th and early 6th centuries BC. Mahajanpadas were the major kingdoms of vedic India during 6th Century BC. Kasi: Varanasi  Kosala: Ayodhya Anga: Champa  Magadha: For a time, Rajgir (known as Rajagriha in the past) was the capital, which was then shifted to Pataliputra  Vajji: Vaishali Malla: Kushinara and Pava Chedi: Sothivati (Near Banda in Uttar Pradesh) Vats

questions.question: Who among the following rulers established the Sunga Dynasty?
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is  Pushyamitra . Key Points The Sunga dynasty was established by Pushyamitra Sunga. Pushyamitra Sunga was a Brahmin. Pushyamitra Sunga was the commander in chief of the Last Mauryan king, Brihadratha. He assassinated Brihadratha in 184 BC. Pushyamitra destroyed many of the Ashokan Stupas and Inscriptions. Agnimitra was the son of Pushyamitra. Bhagabhadra was the son of Agnimitra and Devabhuti was the son of Bhagabhadra. सही उत्तर पुष्यमित्र है।  Key Points

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Stone Age in India:

1. Different periods are identified on the basis of the type and technology of stone tools.

2. There are no regional variations in the type and technology of tools in different periods.

3. Stone Age cultures of different periods evolved uniformly in a near unilinear fashion all over the subcontinent.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution: Solution: The Correct Answer is Option 1 , i.e.  1 only . The stone age is a period defined by the use of tools by a human. The stone age is divided into 3 parts namely Paleolithic (Old Stone Age), Mesolithic (Middle Stone Age) and Neolithic( New Stone Age). Palaeolithic Age: Paleolithic Age was developed in the Pleistocene period.  Robert Bruce Foote was the first person to discover a Paleolithic Stone in India in 1863. questions.question: Svetambara and Digambara are two sects of the _______ community.
questions.solution: Solution: Svetambara and Digambara are two sects of the Jain community. Svetambara Jains are “those who wear white” and is one of the two important sects of Jainism. Svetambaras unlike Digambaras do not believe in renunciation of clothes for attaining liberation. They also believe that anybody can attain liberation(including women). Digamabara Jains are those to whom “space is the garment” and do not wear anything . The  Digambara  Jains worship completely nude

questions.question: Who among the following was the last ruler of Mauryan dynasty?
questions.solution: Solution: Brihadratha was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty. Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty. He defeated the Nanda king Dhanananda with the help of Chanakya/Kautilya. Ashoka was the son of Bindusar and one of the greatest rulers of the Mauryan Empire. Ashoka fought the battle of Kalinga. questions.question: The reign of the ________ dynasty has been described as the golden age of Indian civilization.
questions.solution: Solution: The correct answer is Gupta. The reign of the Gupta dynasty has been described as the golden age of Indian civilization. Key Points  In Ancient India, the Gupta Dynasty ruled the middle of the  3rd century (approximately) to 543 AD. The Gupta dynasty period is referred to as the 'Classical Age or Golden Age of Ancient India. Sri Gupta  was the founder Gupta dynasty Sri Gupta was followed by his son Ghatokkacha and was followed by his son Chandragu
